title: Resolving the quotient by powers of a regular parameter system
statement: Let k be a field, Λ a Noetherian k-algebra and q a prime with Λ_q regular of dimension d [def-weil-regular-scheme] and κ(q)/k separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Let R=k[x_1,...,x_d], φ:R→Λ a k-algebra map whose variable images generate the maximal ideal of Λ_q. For any c≥1, any finitely presented R-algebra C and compatible R-algebra map γ:C→Λ, put J=(x_i^(8c)), J_C=JC and J_Λ=JΛ. Then C/J_C is finitely presented over R/J, there is an induced map γ₀:C/J_C→Λ/J_Λ compatible with γ, and a prime q₀ of Λ/J_Λ whose inverse image is q, such that γ₀ at q₀ can be Popescu resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FE, as repaired in lem-weil-pbc-popescu-resolve-separable

proof.text: Each parameter lies in q by contraction. The inverse image p in R is the origin maximal ideal, with residue field k. Construct the canonical quotient maps and quotient prime; finite presentation descends under base change.

At q the d generators are a regular sequence in the d-dimensional regular local ring. The regular-local polynomial-origin ring has the same dimension. The flat-over-regular lemma makes R_p→Λ_q flat; quotient base change makes the reduced local map flat.

For e=8c, the maximal ideal in R_p/J is nilpotent: degree d(e−1)+1 forces some variable exponent ≥e. Its residue field is k and the target fiber is κ(q). Separability gives that fiber as a filtered colimit of smooth k-algebras. Nilpotent lifting then gives the reduced local target as a filtered colimit of smooth algebras over the reduced local base.
Factor the finitely presented reduced local source through a smooth stage. Its singular ideal is the unit ideal, so this is a local resolution.

The reduced local target has a unique prime because any prime containing the powered parameters contains the maximal ideal. If the reduced singular ideal escapes q₀, the identity is a resolution. Otherwise q₀ is minimal over it and its localization has dimension zero; height-zero delocalization gives the required global quotient resolution. For d=0 both parameter ideals vanish and the local rings are fields.
